purpose: paired exact-state comparison of kernel-localized rolling IPW with standard OPE benchmarks at n=2000
primary_question: How do rolling IPW, exact finite-horizon MIS, and Sequential DR compare as the rapidly forgetting augmented state becomes high-cardinality?

simulator.state: d_x/2 independent binary pairs in {-1,+1}; each pair is (B_j, B_j C_j), with B_j Rademacher and the regime controlling P(C_j=+1)
simulator.policy_design: behavior uses +4.0 g_d(x), target uses -4.0 g_d(x), with identical intercept and embedding term; global sign symmetry gives identical intervention-time laws
simulator.reward: r(x)=0.50+0.35*tanh(2*g_d(x))+0.10*tanh(0.7*h_d(x)); it is state-only, lies in [0.05,0.95], and creates a non-null target-behavior contrast

evaluation.truth_method: exact finite-state dynamic programming over 2^d_x states
evaluation.dr_definition: the same two-fold trajectory-cross-fitted Sequential DR used in Experiment 1, with global time-indexed linear Bellman nuisances and Gaussian-localized held-out scores
evaluation.dr_features: [X,Z,M,A,A*X,A*Z,A*M], with an unpenalized intercept supplied by RidgeCV
evaluation.dr_cross_fitting: two trajectory-level folds; every time-specific penalty is selected by training-fold-only RidgeCV; target truth is never used

selection_protocol.truth_usage: target values are computed independently for scoring only; Sequential DR uses only logged training-fold data
selection_protocol.hyperparameter_selection: Ours, FH-MIS, and the simulator remain fixed; Sequential DR uses the Experiment-1 Ridge grid and training-fold-only RidgeCV
selection_protocol.embedding_selection: ten symmetric central points fixed before the original confirmatory run and all reported with equal weight
selection_protocol.dimension_construction: the d_x=4,8,12 parameter vectors are prefixes of the d_x=16 specification; the final two binary pairs continue the symmetric logit sequence and use opposite equal-norm embedding loadings
selection_protocol.pairing: all methods share the same behavior trajectories within repetition, dimension, sample size, and embedding

analysis_contract.primary_metric: equal-embedding aggregate MSE at each state dimension for n=2000
analysis_contract.primary_comparison: MSE(FH-MIS) and MSE(Sequential DR), each divided by MSE(Ours); values above one favor Ours
secondary_metrics: fraction of target embeddings where Ours has lower MSE
paired mean squared-error difference with a 95% confidence interval
required_plots: RMSE versus state dimension at n=2000
FH-MIS-to-Ours MSE ratio versus state dimension
Sequential-DR-to-Ours MSE ratio versus state dimension
fraction of target embeddings favoring Ours over FH-MIS
